title: Restoring force expression
description: Essential: The response must correctly state the linear restoring force as F ≈ -(mg/L)x or equivalent, showing the small-angle approximation.

title: SHM condition justification
description: Important: The response must explain that motion is SHM because the restoring force is proportional and opposite to displacement, with constant k = mg/L.

title: Period formula derivation
description: Essential: The response must correctly derive and state the final period formula T = 2π√(L/g).

title: Lowest point speed
description: Important: The response must apply energy conservation (or work-energy theorem) to find the speed at the lowest point: v² = 2gL(1 - cosθ).

title: Tension force calculation
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the tension at the lowest point, arriving at F' = mg + (mv²/L) = mg(3 - 2cosθ).

title: Newton's second law application
description: Important: The response must set up Newton's second law at the lowest point: T - mg = m(v²/L), identifying centripetal force.

title: Small-angle assumption
description: Optional: The response may note that the SHM conclusion and period formula are valid only for small angles where sinθ ≈ θ.

title: Sign error in restoring force
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the restoring force expression omits the negative sign indicating direction opposite to displacement.

title: Mass in period formula
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the final pendulum period formula incorrectly includes the mass m (e.g., T = 2π√(m/k) without substituting k correctly).

title: Tension direction mistake
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the net force at the lowest point is incorrectly written (e.g., mg - T = mv²/L) or if centripetal force direction is wrong.
